activity.notes: Frederick succeeded his father as Duke of Swabia in 1147 (as Frederick III). When he was elected Roman-German king in 1152, the Swabian duchy passed to Frederick IV. ATLAS records this pre-royal territorial rule separately from his later royal and imperial offices.

sources.title: Friedrich I. Barbarossa — Neue Deutsche Biographie
sources.citation_text: The German biographical reference identifies Frederick as the son of Duke Frederick II of Swabia and traces his rise before the royal election of 1152.

sources.title: Frederick I Barbarossa, Roman Emperor — Encyclopedia.com
sources.citation_text: The reference biography states that Frederick became Duke of Swabia on his father's death in 1147 and was elected King of Germany in 1152.
